children: slides 8.3% in Thursday's trading as Goldman Sachs initiated coverage with a Neutral rating and $13 price target, expecting tungsten prices to normalize and seeing a more gradual ramp-up than the market expects at the Sangdong mine in South Korea, one of the most important tungsten development assets outside China.

Goldman analyst Nick Cash said Almonty (ALM) sits at the center of the Western tungsten investment narrative, as policy actions taken by China have resulted in global supply concerns, causing the price of tungsten to increase 8x since the beginning of 2025.

shares increasingly reflect a continuation of the current exceptional tungsten market as well as an aggressive production profile for Sangdong, and the analyst said he expects tungsten prices to normalize as new mine supply, recycling, and refining capacity respond to current economics, while Sangdong likely ramps up to progress more gradually than market expectations.
While remaining constructive on the strategic value of Almonty's
asset base, Cash said the current valuation already discounts much of the stock's upside potential.

title: Almonty initiated Neutral at Goldman as valuation already discounts company's potential
